content: 1. Isavuconazonium sulfate and lumateperone: Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the plasma levels and effects of lumateperone by inhibiting CYP3A4-mediated hepatic and intestinal metabolism. When co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the lumateperone dose to 21 mg/day. Close monitoring is required. 2. Lurasidone and isavuconazonium sulfate: Lurasidone increases the levels and effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 3. Lurbinectedin and isavuconazonium sulfate: Both drugs reduce immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Isavuconazonium sulfate and mavacamten: Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the levels and effects of mavacamten by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Initiation of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may necessitate a reduction in the mavacamten dose. Close monitoring is essential. 5. Mavorixafor and isavuconazonium sulfate: Mavorixafor increases the levels and effects of isavuconazonium sulfate via CYP3A4 inhibition. Conversely, isavuconazonium sulfate increases mavorixafor levels through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Adjust therapy as needed and monitor for adverse effects. 6. Mechlorethamine and isavuconazonium sulfate: Both drugs reduce immunosuppressive effects, heightening the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Mefloquine and isavuconazonium sulfate: Mefloquine increases the levels and effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 8. Melphalan and isavuconazonium sulfate: Both drugs reduce immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Memantine and isavuconazonium sulfate: Isavuconazonium sulfate, as an OCT2 inhibitor, may increase the levels and effects of memantine. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor closely. 10. Mercaptopurine and isavuconazonium sulfate: Both drugs reduce immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Methimazole and isavuconazonium sulfate: Methimazole increases the levels and effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Methoxsalen and isavuconazonium sulfate: Methoxsalen increases the levels and effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Methylprednisolone and isavuconazonium sulfate: Methylprednisolone increases the levels and effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs reduce immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Metronidazole and isavuconazonium sulfate: Metronidazole increases the levels and effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Micafungin and isavuconazonium sulfate: Micafungin increases the levels and effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Midazolam and isavuconazonium sulfate: Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the levels and effects of midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Mifepristone and isavuconazonium sulfate: Mifepristone significantly increases the levels and effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated.
